generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The implementation of `validateCharSequenceToken` contains a logic error when handling non-ASCII characters. By casting `token.charAt(i)` directly to a `byte`, characters with values greater than 255 (e.g., Unicode characters) are truncated to their lowest 8 bits. If these lower 8 bits correspond to a valid token character, the validator will incorrectly return that the character is valid. For example, the character `\u0121` (decimal 289) would be cast to byte 33 (`'!'`), which is a valid token character. To fix this, you should explicitly check if `token.charAt(i) > 127` before casting or performing the bitset lookup.
